Q: Issue with out-variable decleration refernce outside the contain block A:

My revised answer:

GetCustomAttribute<T>(MemberInfo, Boolean) is an Extension Method of the System.Reflection.MethodInfo class. An extension method is type of static method that you can use to decorate an existing class. In this case, MemberInfo doesn't natively have a method GetCustomAttribute<T>(MemberInfo, Boolean) just as your error message states. The only way to access that is through System.Reflection not the base class.

See doc: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.reflection.methodinfo?view=netframework-4.8.1

The fix is either to add;

using System.Reflection; // to the namespace

or fully qualify the extension method when used:

MiniscriptFunctionAttribute? attribute = System.Reflection.CustomAttributeExtensions.GetCustomAttribute<MiniscriptFunctionAttribute>(methodInfo);

Additionally I still think the if statement should be negated as your logic is essentially "if found, throw exception that function is not found" and while permissible I'm still not a fan of the leaked scope style variable declaration. Call it personal preference, but I don't like it.

As to why it's sometimes throwing the error and sometimes not, I think that's actually a function of you making changes and the IDE's backend processing adding imports on the fly as you're trying to facilitate autocomplete or IntelliSense or something and you end up getting an implied "using System.Reflection;" added to the code behind the scenes while it's doing it's thing. Could be wrong on that, but ultimately I think this simply trying to call a method that isn't in scope because your code incorrectly assumes it's part of the type.

Q: How can I get NPM to ignore package versions newer than a threshold by default? A:

First you update your NPM to 11+
npm install -g npm@latest

Then in your project root create a file ".npmrc" or next to your package-json.
Set in the file this line:
min-release-age=90

Now if you install ie lets say "threejs" with npm install three@latest, it will "gate" the version to ie. 180 instead of the newest 184, and all dependencies as well. So this way you cant have any package newer than the 90 day threshold.
You can try it out to see it if works, by setting age to 300 and see if it downgrades your package to a much older version.

From NPM documentation
"min-release-age
If set, npm will build the npm tree such that only versions that were available more than the given number of days ago will be installed. If there are no versions available for the current set of dependencies, the command will error."

Q: Filter data table for multiple condition in UiPath A:

You can use Datatable.Select to filter a datatable with multiple conditions fairly easily.

myDataTable.Select("[Column x] Not in ('value1', 'value2', 'value3')")

Will give you all the DataRows where the field in your datatable called Column X is not value1, value2, or value3

Q: How to use google drive file list api with drive API Key without oAuth2.0? A:

API keys are not sufficient for your goal. API keys are solely for authorization (ie. "you may make this API call"), they cannot do authentication (ie. "you are yourname@gmail.com"). Without authentication, you're trying to ask this API method "show me all files which match my search" and it is rejecting your request because there can't be any files which match that search for everyone (since files are organized in accounts).

OAuth 2.0 does both authorization (identifies your Google Cloud project as having enabled this API) and authentication (identifies your end-user account, with your permission, so it knows who is making the call), so the API knows what files belong to you and thus what results to return.

As such, the Google Drive API requires OAuth 2.0 authorization (see here).
